newsitem.title: GERMANY: BT says mulls bid for Spain's Retevision.
newsitem.headline: BT says mulls bid for Spain's Retevision.

text.p: British Telecommunications said on Thursday it was mulling a potential bid for Spain's Retevision SA, a broadcaster based in Madrid.
"We are considering whether or not to bid for Retevision," Patrick Gallagher, BT's managing director for Europe, told Reuters after a news conference with BT's German partner Viag.

Retevision, Spain's second telecommunications operator after Telefonica de Espana SA, is due to be fully privatised by 2000. Spain intends to sell initially between 51-60 percent of its share capital.
Among those likely to compete for the sale is a consortium formed by Endesa, Banco Central Hispano and Banco Santander.

Multinational consortium Global One -- comprising France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and America's Sprint -- as well as BT and Britain's Cable & Wireless have been tipped by newspapers to have shown an interest.
Earlier this month, Deutsche Telekom declined to confirm or deny reports that it planned to bid for a stake in the Spanish broadcaster along with France Telecom.
